title: This Is the Year of Value
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Dave Stuart Jr. argues that in the wake of the pandemic and the rapid spread of generative AI, cultivating students' sense of the Value of learning has become the decisive work of teaching, more urgent than relationship-building alone. He pushes back on the popular claim that "school is all about relationships," insisting that schools exist specifically to grow students toward mastery of academic disciplines, and that relational capital must be spent developing the other Five Key Beliefs rather than treated as sufficient on its own. He traces how American schools have leaned almost exclusively on utility and relevance to justify learning's worth, a narrow strategy that collapses once students are awash in algorithmic engagement machines and AI tools. Drawing on the research behind The Will to Learn, he introduces the "Rainbow of Why" as a fuller set of avenues — beauty, pleasure, meaning, autonomy, justice, purpose — through which teachers can help students value coursework beyond mere usefulness. He predicts that schools which deliberately invest in Value cultivation, whether AI-embracing or AI-resistant, will pull ahead of schools that don't, and offers three concrete starting points: apologetic mini-sermons, knowledge-rich curricula, and Valued Within exercises.
points: Stuart argues relational capital (MGCs, "Every Student Known") is necessary but insufficient — it must be actively spent cultivating the Value belief, not treated as the endpoint of good teaching.
He names AI and smartphone-driven "algorithmic engagement machines" as the forces exposing the weakness of school's traditional utility/relevance-only case for learning.
The "Rainbow of Why," built from a decade of motivation research for The Will to Learn, reframes Value cultivation around beauty, meaning, autonomy, justice, and purpose rather than just usefulness.
He predicts a coming "separation" between schools that intentionally cultivate Value and those that don't, regardless of each school's AI policy.
Three practical levers he recommends: apologetic mini-sermons, knowledge-rich curricula, and Valued Within exercises that help students locate personal meaning in coursework.
quotes: But parents don't send their children to school just to have relationships. They send them to school to learn things — to grow toward mastery.

So what happens when a culture obsessed with utility and relevance gets flooded with magical algorithmic engagement machines (smartphones) in the 2010s and sophisticated AI tools in the 2020s? The Value of school plummets.

It is my view that in this coming school year and the few that follow, schools that double down on Value cultivation will separate themselves from schools that do not. Some of these schools will lean heavily on AI; others will forbid its use completely.
Value cultivation is hard, for sure. Especially with the AI-related changes to culture and work and school that none of us opted-in for.
Value cultivation has always been an important skill set with great rewards. The more we help our students value the work of learning, the more they'll be drawn to do that work with care.

Schools have always struggled to help students genuinely believe that learning is good. In ultra-pragmatic and individualistic cultures like the United States, schools tend to heavily rely on the Value avenues of utility and relevance.
